reproduction_target: SNPBag, a BERT-architecture foundation model (836 M parameters, 16 encoder layers x 16 attention heads, 512-dim embedding, sliding-window attention) pre-trained by masked-genotype prediction on 1 million synthetic human genomes covering 6,030,514 SNP sites, plus the benchmark pipeline built around it: RESHAPE-based simulation of 1 M chr22 genotype sequences from 1000 Genomes 30x samples, HAPNEST-based simulation of 1 M whole genomes, chr22 and whole-genome pre-training, fine-tuning for genotype imputation (Illumina Omni2.5 masking, evaluated on 216 HGDP individuals) and for haplotype phasing (switch-error rate on 26 physically phased HGDP genomes), comparison against conventional phasing/imputation pipelines (SHAPEIT4 / BEAGLE5.2 / EAGLE2 x IMPUTE5 / MINIMAC4 / BEAGLE5.2 following De Marino et al.), genome-embedding head training (2,934 contigs x 128 dims), population classification on 3,202 1kG individuals, and ped-sim-based relatedness inference. The study is entirely computational; no wet-lab work is reported. Boundary call: this could equally be routed 'hybrid', since the paper both ships a tool (public inference code + two demo web services) and reports application-style benchmark results; 'tool-methods' was chosen because the central claim is the model/framework itself and the repository is organised as per-task reproduction code.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, derived from the six Methods subsections (Base model pre-training, Genotype imputation, Haplotype phasing, Genome embedding, Population classification, Relatedness inference). The two training-data simulations are separate steps because they use different generators and different source cohorts (C1 RESHAPE from 1kG 30x; C2 HAPNEST from 1kG + HGDP), and the two pre-trainings are separate steps because they are two distinct models with different site counts and window sizes (C3 chr22, C4 whole-genome). The conventional imputation/phasing comparison (C6) is kept separate from the SNPBag imputation benchmark (C5) because it is an entirely different toolchain with different disclosure. ped-sim pedigree simulation (C10) is separate from the relatedness classifier (C11) as a distinct named tool invocation. The repository landing page shows two directories with no corresponding Methods prose ('scaling', and an undocumented 'whole-genome_pretrain'); no step was created for 'scaling' because the step list is prose-anchored. No wet-lab steps: W = 0.

steps.label: Simulation of 1 million chr22 phased genotype sequences ('the RESHAPE data') from the 3,202 samples of the 1000 Genomes Project 30x high-coverage dataset using RESHAPE software: individuals grouped into 5 super-populations (African, Admixed American, East Asian, European, South Asian) as ancestors, 8th-generation offspring simulated within each super-population

Whole-genome training cohort construction: 1 million synthetic genomes from the HAPNEST project (1kG and HGDP samples as ancestors) and SNP-site selection - structural variants excluded, only SNP sites shared between 1kG and HGDP with 1kG minor allele frequency > 1% retained, yielding 6,030,514 sites organised into consecutive per-chromosome contigs of 1,024-81,920 sites

Pre-training of the chromosome-22 base model: BERT encoder, 16 bidirectional transformer layers x 16 attention heads, 512-dim linear input projection, sliding-window attention of 256 tokens, input sequence 81,920 tokens (~92% of chr22; first 6,000 and last 967 sites excluded), genotypes coded 0/1/2 with mask token 3, 85-99% of positions randomly masked, MLP decoder, cross-entropy loss against unmasked genotypes; trained on the 1 M RESHAPE sequences from C1

Pre-training of the whole-genome base model (~836 million parameters): same BERT architecture with sliding-window attention of 128 tokens, trained on the 1 M HAPNEST synthetic genomes over the 6,030,514 selected sites; used downstream for genome embedding, population classification and distant relatedness inference

Genotype-imputation benchmark of SNPBag: chr22, 81,920 sites of which 16,230 (20%) are on the Illumina Omni2.5 array and 80% are masked per the Omni2.5 design; evaluated on complete genotype sequences from 216 HGDP individuals (4 randomly selected per each of 54 populations). Two variants: 'SNPBag base' (pre-trained chr22 model applied directly) and 'SNPBag omni' (chr22 model fine-tuned on the RESHAPE data with Omni2.5-aligned masking patterns). Accuracy stratified by MAF bins (equal-site-count intervals) and continental groupings

Conventional imputation comparison arm: 'pipelines benchmarked by De Marino et al.', combining phasing (SHAPEIT4, BEAGLE5.2 or EAGLE2, with or without the 1kG reference panel) with imputation (IMPUTE5, MINIMAC4 or BEAGLE5.2), run on the same Omni2.5-masked HGDP sequences

Haplotype phasing: chr22 base model fine-tuned on 1 million phased genotype sequences synthesized via RESHAPE from 1kG samples, taking unphased genotypes as input with a new MLP decoder predicting allelic-state switches (ancestral/derived) between adjacent heterozygous sites, cross-entropy loss against true switch sequences; evaluated by switch error rate on 26 physically phased HGDP genomes against SHAPEIT4 / BEAGLE5.2 / EAGLE2 with and without the 1kG reference panel

Genome-embedding head training: whole-genome base model fine-tuned with each genome segmented into 2,934 contigs of 2,048 SNPs, contig sequences randomly masked at 75-85% of sites, encoder output (2,048 x 512) compressed by two sequential MLPs (sequence 2,048 -> 16; model dim 512 -> 8) and flattened to a 128-dim contig embedding, a third MLP predicting the 2,048 genotypes from the contig embedding, optimised by cross-entropy until 95% genotype-recovery accuracy; contig embeddings concatenated into a 2,934 x 128 genome embedding (0.75 MB per genome)

Population classification: lightweight neural network of three MLPs (two reducing the 2,934 x 128 genome embedding to a 6 x 6 representation, a third projecting onto 19 population categories defined by Gaspar and Breen 2019) trained on genome embeddings of 3,202 1kG individuals with their population labels; assessed by 10 iterations of 5-fold cross-validation with random 4:1 training/test partitioning, F1 and other metrics averaged across iterations; repeated for all 26 1kG populations

Pedigree simulation for relatedness inference with ped-sim software: 14 of the 26 populations among the 2,504 unrelated individuals of the 1kG phase-3 panel selected for low admixture, each split into training and test sets with test sets fixed at 20 individuals, 40 pedigree trees simulated for training and 4 for testing per population, each tree spanning 11 generations with 40 individuals (20 1kG genomes + 20 synthetic genomes), capturing pairwise relatedness from degree 1 to 19 plus unrelated pairs; yielding 12,320 synthetic genomes, 759,327 training pairs and 73,345 test pairs

Relatedness classification: SNPBag genome embeddings generated for the simulated pedigree individuals, pairs of embeddings combined and classified by a lightweight neural network of MLPs for dimensionality reduction and classification (detection of genetic relationships up to 12th-degree relatives)

headline.static_readiness: 0/11 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification); unexecuted, and under-claiming by construction since Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency. n_exact_capture_unexecuted = 0, n_fetch_required = 0.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 0/11 (0%). Even the most generous inference-inclusive reading yields no RI step, because the Version axis is 0 for every SNPBag-side step: the paper names no version for any software it used (no Python, PyTorch, CUDA, RESHAPE or ped-sim version anywhere in Methods), the repository carries no tag and no release, and the README documents no dependencies, no requirements file, no conda environment and no container. The only version-bearing strings in the whole paper are the third-party comparison tools of C6 (SHAPEIT4, BEAGLE5.2, EAGLE2, IMPUTE5, MINIMAC4), which are major-version labels rather than exact pins, and that step fails instead on Params (no command lines or flags given for any of the six tool combinations). The binding constraints are therefore, in order: (1) total absence of any software-version or environment declaration, (2) absence of the trained model weights, without which the inference-only code that the paper does publish cannot be run at all, and (3) absence of a Data Availability / Code Availability statement, so the GitHub URL appears only in the Introduction body text.
headline.coverage: 11 computational steps assessed from the six Methods subsections of the v3 JATS full text, plus the single in-text artifact statement ('we have made the model inference publicly available on GitHub (https://github.com/augix/SNPBag)') and the repository landing page and README prose. The paper has no Data Availability section and no Code Availability section. No wet-lab steps (W = 0); the study is entirely computational. Supplementary figures were not fetched at stage 1.

gaps.where: Software environment across all 11 computational steps
gaps.missing: No software version is stated anywhere for the authors' own stack. Methods name RESHAPE and ped-sim with no version; no deep-learning framework, Python version, CUDA version or hardware specification is given for a 836 M-parameter model trained on 6 trillion tokens. The repository root contains no requirements.txt, environment.yml, conda-lock, pixi.lock, Dockerfile or setup file, and the README has no installation or dependency section at all. Only the third-party comparison tools of C6 carry major-version labels (SHAPEIT4, BEAGLE5.2, EAGLE2, IMPUTE5, MINIMAC4).
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a resolved environment (conda-lock / pixi.lock / container digest) pinning interpreter, framework, CUDA and channel/index for the training and inference stack, and state the exact versions of RESHAPE, ped-sim and each comparison tool with their command lines.

gaps.where: Trained model weights for both base models (C3, C4) and for all five fine-tuned task heads (C5, C7, C8, C9, C11)
gaps.missing: No checkpoint, weights archive or model registry entry is stated anywhere in the paper or the README. The abstract and Introduction advertise public availability of 'the model inference' only. The sole way to obtain model outputs is through two demo web services hosted on bare IP addresses (http://112.124.68.206:5000 and http://121.40.50.52:5000), which are unversioned, non-archival, and one of which is already unreachable. Since the paper's compute scale (1 M genomes, 6 trillion tokens) puts retraining out of reach for almost any third party, the missing weights are the single largest barrier to any reproduction attempt.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the base-model and task-head checkpoints under a persistent identifier (HuggingFace model repo with a pinned revision, or Zenodo with a DOI), record the checksum in the paper, and cite it from a Code and Data Availability statement.

gaps.missing: The paper carries no Data Availability section and no Code Availability section. The single artifact statement is a URL embedded in the Introduction narrative. The repository has no tag, no release, no license file, and no Zenodo/Software Heritage archival snapshot, so there is no way to identify which state of the code corresponds to the v3 manuscript (repository created 2025-08-27, last push 2025-12-17, i.e. after the v3 posting date of 2025-10-11).
gaps.how_to_close: Add a Code and Data Availability section, cut a tagged release matching the manuscript version, archive it to Zenodo for a DOI, and add a license.

gaps.where: Input datasets for C1, C2, C5, C7, C9, C10
gaps.missing: No accession, DOI or download URL is given for any input dataset. The 1000 Genomes 30x high-coverage callset (3,202 samples), the 1kG phase-3 panel (2,504 unrelated individuals), the HGDP callset (929 samples), the physically phased HGDP subset (26 genomes) and the HAPNEST synthetic cohort (1 M genomes) are all referred to by project name and citation only. A full-text scan found no GEO, SRA, ENA, ArrayExpress, dbGaP, EGA, figshare, Zenodo or Dryad identifier anywhere in the article. The derived 6,030,514-site list, the 1 M RESHAPE sequences and the 1 M HAPNEST-derived training genomes are likewise not deposited.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact release/accession and access URL for each source callset (e.g. the 1kG 30x release identifier, the HGDP release, the HAPNEST distribution DOI) and deposit the derived site list and the simulated training cohorts, or the exact scripts and seeds that regenerate them.

gaps.where: C5 (216 HGDP evaluation individuals), C7 (26 physically phased HGDP genomes), C10 (14 of 26 1kG populations, per-population train/test splits)
gaps.missing: None of the evaluation sample sets is enumerated. C5 says '216 out of 929 independent HGDP samples' and '4 randomly selected individuals per 54 populations' without listing the IDs or a seed; C7 names no IDs for the 26 physically phased genomes; C10 says '14 of 26 populations were selected for their low levels of admixture' without naming them, and fixes test sets at 20 individuals per population without listing which. Benchmark numbers therefore cannot be recomputed on the same samples.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the sample-ID manifests (evaluation individuals, phased genomes, selected populations, train/test partitions) as a supplementary table or a file in the repository.

gaps.missing: Every stochastic operation in the study is reported without a random seed: RESHAPE and ped-sim pedigree simulation, the 85-99% random genotype masking in pre-training, the 75-85% random contig masking for embeddings, the random selection of 4 individuals per HGDP population, and the random 4:1 partitioning in the 10 x 5-fold cross-validation. No seed, RNG library or determinism setting (e.g. deterministic cuDNN kernels) is stated, so even with weights and code in hand only distributional agreement, not bitwise agreement, could be claimed.
gaps.how_to_close: Record and publish the seeds for each simulation and training run, and state the determinism settings used for GPU training.

gaps.where: C6 conventional imputation and phasing comparison arm
gaps.missing: The entire comparison arm is delegated to an external reference: 'Conventional imputation followed pipelines benchmarked by De Marino et al.'. No command line, parameter set, reference-panel build or wrapper script is given for any of the six phasing x imputation combinations, and no corresponding directory is visible on the repository landing page.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the actual invocation scripts for each phasing/imputation combination, with tool versions, reference-panel identity and full flag sets.

gaps.where: C1, C2, C3, C10 - data simulation, site selection and chr22 pre-training
gaps.missing: The in-text statement scopes the public release to 'the model inference'. The repository landing page lists task directories (emb, imputation, phasing, pop_classifier, relatedness) that the README describes as 'code for reproducing figures on the manuscript', plus two undocumented directories (whole-genome_pretrain, scaling). No directory corresponds to the RESHAPE simulation, the MAF-based site-selection procedure, the ped-sim pedigree generation, or the chr22 pre-training, so those steps are reconstructable from prose at best.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the simulation, site-selection and pre-training drivers (including the chr22 model) with their configuration files, and document the currently undocumented directories in the README.

gaps.where: Demo inference services advertised in the README
gaps.missing: Of the three demo endpoints listed, one is already struck through by the authors as retired, and server0 (http://112.124.68.206:5000) did not respond within a 12 s timeout on 2026-07-28; only server1 (http://121.40.50.52:5000) returned 200. These are bare-IP, unversioned endpoints with no archival guarantee - they are the only functional access path to the trained model and they are the most perishable artifact in the record. No redundancy rescue is possible because there is no authoritative mirror.
gaps.how_to_close: Replace or supplement the demo endpoints with an archived model deposit under a persistent identifier.
